external_ids: buyer-ref:centre for environment, fisheries and aquaculture science:CEFAS26-109
title: CEFAS26-109 RFQ for Sediment Coring Survey Services aboard RV Cefas Endeavour
description: Cefas requires the provision of specialist marine geotechnical services to support two vibracoring surveys within the Irish Sea Firth of Clyde or North Sea. The Supplier is required to achieve sediment cores each with a target penetration of up to 3 m from pre-planned stations for the delivery of our environmental sampling programme. The Supplier is required to provide a 3 metre vibrocorer, complete with spares, coring consumables (coring liners etc) core splitting and core cutting equipment, and suitable individuals to undertake operations of the vibrocorer on a 24 hrs period (2 x 12 hrs shifts back-to-back) alongside deck crew. The Supplier’s personnel will be accommodated onboard the RV Cefas Endeavour for the duration of the survey. Cefas will provide suitable onboard cabin accommodation, bedding and welfare facilities, together with meals and refreshments as part of the vessel’s normal catering provision. The RV Cefas Endeavour has en-suite accommodation for scientific and technical personnel. The Supplier should therefore not include separate accommodation or subsistence costs for periods spent onboard the vessel. Any specific dietary requirements should be notified to Cefas in advance of mobilisation. The Supplier will remain responsible for all travel and associated costs required to mobilise and demobilise its personnel and equipment to/from the agreed port, unless otherwise stated. This should be reflected in the quote provided. The survey is scheduled for approximately ten to twelve days between the 1st to the 16th of November with the flexibility of +/- 5 days each side, with the availability to mobilise and demobilise equipment either in Lowestoft or a Port on the Southwest coast. The port will be confirmed by Cefas as soon as possible. Suppliers must be prepared to mobilise and demobilise from either location. Suppliers must provide evidence of valid and appropriate offshore survival training and medical certification, including BOSIET or STCW95 and a UK Offshore Operators Association-approved medical, or suitable equivalents. Original hard copies of all required certification and documentation will be required for inspection upon request at the time of vessel mobilisation. Please note general arrangement drawings of the RV Cefas Endeavour can be supplied upon Contract award for operational logistics if required. Requirement: The Supplier will liaise with Cefas before mobilisation to confirm the operational requirements, vessel interfaces, equipment layout, power supply, lifting arrangements, programme and health and safety requirements. A mobilisation plan shall be prepared and agreed by both parties in advance of installation. The Supplier will provide a fully maintained and function-tested 3 m high-powered vibrocorer spread, including its control system, constant-tension winch, core barrels, workshop container, essential spares and associated ancillary equipment. The proposed system shall be suitable for operations in water depths of approximately 150 m. The vibrocorer spread shall be delivered to the nominated mobilisation port and installed aboard the RV Cefas Endeavour. Following installation, the Supplier will complete appropriate equipment inspections, function tests and deployment checks, including a wet test where practicable. The Supplier will provide suitably trained and experienced equipment technicians to install, operate, maintain and demobilise the vibrocoring equipment. The base provision shall comprise of four technicians for operations of up to 24 hours per day (two technicians per 12-hour shift). The two technicians will be supported by RV Cefas Endeavour crew for the safe deployment and recovery of equipment. At each survey location, the vessel shall establish a safe and stable working position before the vibrocorer is deployed to the seabed using the vessel’s suitable crane or A-frame and lifting winch. Cefas shall provide the station position and water-depth information for each deployment. Once seabed conditions and the survey position have been confirmed, the vibrocorer shall be operated until either: • the full available barrel penetration is achieved; • refusal is encountered due to the ground conditions; or • the deployment is stopped for operational or safety reasons. Following each attempt, the vibrocorer shall be recovered to deck and the retained sediment core removed from the barrel, visually inspected, split and transferred to Cefas personnel. The Supplier will undertake the acquisition of the sediment cores and check the samples and associated acquisition information before handing them to Cefas. Unless otherwise agreed, laboratory testing, detailed data processing, interpretation, and reporting are outside the Suppliers scope. The Supplier will maintain the vibrocorer spread throughout the offshore programme and provide suitable spare parts for key components to minimise operational downtime. Any equipment defects shall be reported promptly to the Cefas Survey Lead, together with proposed corrective action and any expected effect on the programme. The proposed provision includes full spares coverage for key components. On completion of the offshore work, the Supplier will safely isolate, dismantle and remove its equipment from the vessel at the nominated demobilisation port. The work area shall be left in a safe and satisfactory condition. The Supplier will carry out the Services in accordance with its approved health and safety and quality-management procedures, Cefas vessel requirements and all applicable legislation, including the Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998 (LOLER), where applicable. All offshore activities shall be appropriately risk assessed, and suitable method statements, lifting plans and operational procedures shall be agreed before mobilisation. All lifting equipment and accessories shall be suitable for the intended operation, appropriately certified and subject to the required examination and inspection regime. Download the Bidder Pack at https://defra-family.force.com/s/Welcome and search for CEFAS26-109 under opportunities.

title: Provision of The Drive Project
description: The Office of the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Northamptonshire is seeking to commission a specialist provider to deliver the DRIVE Project. The Drive Project is a response to domestic abuse that aims to reduce the number of child and adult victims of domestic abuse by disrupting and changing perpetrator behaviour. It implements a whole-system approach through an intensive individual case management intervention alongside a co-ordinated multi-agency response to drive perpetrators to change their behaviour. The Drive Project focuses on increasing victim safety alongside the crucial protective work of victims’ services. The service has been developed to knit together existing services, complementing and enhancing existing interventions. PME was not undertaken as part of this procurement as The Drive Project is a national project with a pre-determined specification.

title: GOV Voice
description: The Gov Voice programme, led by the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, is focused on establishing a cross-government, AI-enabled voice capability to modernise how citizens interact with public sector contact services. It centres on deploying generative AI voice technology as a core component of a more integrated and consistent approach to service delivery across organisations. A key aim of the programme is to enhance the overall citizen experience by enabling automated handling of routine enquiries. This approach is designed to reduce wait times, improve accessibility, and provide quicker resolutions for common queries, supporting a more responsive interface with government services. Alongside these user benefits, the programme introduces a reusable and scalable platform that can be adopted across multiple organisations. By providing a centrally assured solution, it reduces duplication of effort and enables a more efficient, coordinated model for delivering voice-based services at scale. Crucially, while led centrally, Gov Voice is intended to be applicable across the whole public sector landscape, enabling adoption by central government departments, local government organisations, and Arm’s Length Bodies (ALBs) to provide a consistent, interoperable voice capability that can operate securely within government environments and scale across multiple services.

Through this engagement, the Council wishes to better understand: (i)The availability of suitable premises within the borough. title: ITT for the Provision of Social Media Management Tool
description: Energy Saving Trust owns over 38 social media accounts across various channels. To manage all the accounts effectively, we need a powerful social media management tool. As our social media presence continues to grow, we would like to evaluate the tools available in the market and select the best tool that is in line with our budget and can empower us to achieve our marketing goals. Lot 1: . Energy Saving Trust owns 42 social media accounts across various channels. To manage all the accounts effectively, we need a powerful social media management tool. As our social media presence continues to grow, we would like to evaluate tools available in the market and select the best tool that is in line with our budget and can empower us to achieve our marketing goals. Please refer to below for requirements. Role of the Contractor Provide all of the “essential” requirements and any or all of the “value-added” of the social media management tool requirements and specifications listed in the ITT: Scheduling: Essential - Simple scheduling process (including multimedia posts) - Scheduling across multiple platforms (including story scheduling) - Reel scheduling with Instagram grid option - Filing posts by campaign - Post preview - Save as drafts - Repost evergreen content - Content approvals - Accept multiple image/video formats - Add alt text Reporting: Essential - Overview of paid and organic post-performance across platforms - Engagement metrics: likes, shares, comments, saves, reactions - Reach and impressions tracking (paid vs. organic) - Follower growth over time - Click-through rates (CTR) for links in posts - Video views and watch time - Campaign-level performance reporting - Platform-specific breakdowns - Exportable reports (e.g., PDF, CSV) - Custom date range selection - Top-performing content identification - Audience demographics overview - Paid media spend and ROI tracking - Cost-per-click (CPC), cost-per-impression (CPM), and conversion metrics Value added Provides clear insights into both paid and organic performance. Helping teams access quick reporting tools to make informed decisions on campaign activity. Social listening and brand mentions Essential - Real-time monitoring of brand mentions across platforms - Sentiment analysis of audience conversations - Keyword and hashtag tracking - Competitor mention tracking - Influencer and media coverage alerts - In-depth reporting for posts and inbox messages - Campaign-level analytics Social community management and engagement: Essential - Ability to respond to inbox messages and comments across platforms (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok, BlueSky) - Unified inbox for monitoring comments, mentions, and messages - Reporting on number of messages responded to - Assign messages to specific team members or platform users - Forward messages and comments via email - View full message history from users - Add and manage customisable tags for message categorisation Governance and Team Management: Essential - Granular control over user access and permissions - Ability to assign roles based on responsibilities (e.g. content creator, approver, analyst) - Audit trail of user activity for accountability (e.g compliance and audit) - Centralised management of social media accounts - Ability to manage multiple teams or departments within the platform - Customisable workflows for approvals and publishing Customer support and training: Essential - Availability of customer support for troubleshooting and assistance - Access to training materials and resources (tutorials, user guides, FAQs) - Onboarding sessions or training programs provided by the vendor - Dedicated account manager for ongoing support and queries IT security and GDPR Essential - Server infrastructure must comply with UK GDPR requirements - Data must be stored and processed securely within approved jurisdictions - Platform must support secure user authentication and access controls - Ability to archive and retrieve communications for compliance purposes - Clear data handling policies aligned with FCA and ICO expectations - Support for data subject access requests (DSARs) and deletion requests - ISO/IEC 27001 certification or SOC2.

title: Quality Assurance and Testing for IT Systems 2
description: Quality Assurance and Testing for IT Systems 2 Independent quality assurance testing (QAT), including testing environments, specialists, automation and services, such as consultancy. Updates 13 June 2025: This framework agreement has been extended to expire 23 February 2029. New suppliers will still be able to join the DPS up until this date. Description The framework will use a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) to offer independent quality assurance testing (QAT) services for use by the whole of the public sector and their associated bodies and agencies. QAT is needed for new digital systems and services to make sure they are suitable for public launch. The agreement offers services such as: testing environments specialists automation services (such as consultancy) Benefits it complements our other digital agreements, such as Digital Outcomes and Specialists (DOS) and G-Cloud dynamic – buyers can create bespoke specifications (within the overall DPS scope), competitions and contracts state your requirements and suppliers tell you how they’ll deliver the service government owned Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), means that you can continue to develop a digital service yourself or with any third party, or share and reuse it Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Quality Assurance and Testing for IT Systems 2 Expires: 23/02/2029 How to buy You must run a mini competition to select a supplier. There is no option for direct award. Before you run your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the DPS marketplace. This DPS is organised into 4 categories: services location clearance scalability The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the DPS marketplace. Although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Quality Assurance and Testing for IT Systems 2 DPS under Technology and choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. when creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet). Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a further Competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. the list is valid for only 2 working days , from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point. if your call for competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations you will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export you can use the our eSourcing tool to run a call for competition. The tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing sufficient time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a 2-day deadline for submitting evidence . If you are satisfied with the evidence, award the contract Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder . Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. Documents published before this date may still refer to CCS. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. title: HH065-25-HB Medical Services HMP Highland
description: NHS Highland and the Scottish Prison Service (SPS) require a Medical Service for individuals held at the new HMP Highland, Prison due to open in Spring 2027. The service will support the delivery of safe, effective and person centred healthcare within a custodial environment and must align with NHS clinical governance, statutory responsibilities, and prison healthcare standards. Lot 1: . The contract will cover the delivery of routine and urgent primary medical care, continuity of care, and appropriate liaison with NHS Highland services and partner organisations. The service is critical to ensuring equitable access to healthcare for a vulnerable population and must operate within the constraints of a secure setting, requiring close collaboration with operational prison staff and adherence to information governance, data protection, and safeguarding requirements.. Given the specialist nature of custodial healthcare and workforce pressures within primary care, the procurement must ensure service resilience, quality, and continuity throughout the contract term.
eligibility_text: Bidders are required to provide examples that demonstrate that they have the relevant experience to deliver the services as described in part II.2.4 of the Find a Tender Service Contract Notice or the relevant section of the Site Notice. Bidders are required to confirm they and/or the service provider have the following relevant professional qualifications: Provide evidence of registration with regulatory body such as the GMC for all GPs who will be working on this contract. Quality Management Procedures 1.The bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent) accredited independent third party certificate of compliance in accordance with BS ISO 45001 (or equivalent), Or, 2. The bidder must have the following: a. A documented policy regarding quality management. The policy must set out responsibilities for quality management demonstrating that the bidder has, and continues to implement, a quality management policy that is authorised by their Chief Executive, or equivalent, which is periodically reviewed at a senior management level. The policy must be relevant to the nature and scale of the work to be undertaken and set out responsibilities for quality management throughout the organisation. Health and Safety Procedures 3. The bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent), accredited independent third party certificate of compliance in accordance with BS OHSAS 18001 (or equivalent) or have, within the last 12 months, successfully met the assessment requirements of a construction-related scheme in registered membership of the Safety Schemes in Procurement (SSIP) forum. The Bidder must hold a UKAS (or equivalent) accredited independent third party certificate of compliance with BS EN ISO 14001 (or equivalent) or a valid EMAS (or equivalent) certificate, or a regularly reviewed documented process.

title: Market Engagement Notice for the Provision of FMS Managed Services
description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

title: Provision of Corporate and Professional Services to Big Life Schools Multi Academy Trust
description: The Trust is seeking a single strategic partner to deliver an integrated suite of corporate and professional services that enable school leaders to focus on educational outcomes while ensuring the Trust operates efficiently, safely, compliantly and sustainably. The successful supplier will provide integrated professional support services that are reliable, compliant, responsive and strategically aligned to the Trust’s objectives, through a single accountable management structure combining strategic advice, operational delivery, performance management, continuous improvement and innovation. The Services comprise the following ten service areas, described in full in the Specification: Financial Services- Operational and transactional financial management, management accounts, 5-year planning, VAT/ONS returns and audit liaison (Sage 200; circa 20,000 transactions per year). Payroll Services - Payroll processing and system for circa 200 staff (pay date 15th), RTI/HMRC, Teachers’ Pension and Local Government Pension Scheme administration. Human Resources Services - Operational HR, recruitment, employee relations, policy development, TUPE advice and the staff wellbeing offer. Staff Training & Development - Mandatory and wider training (safeguarding, cyber, H&S and more), CPD support and maintenance of Trust accreditations. Legal Services (incl. employment) - Operational and strategic legal support on contracts, employment and H&S matters, from suitably regulated advisers. Managed ICT Services- Secure, resilient network, servers, connectivity, filtering, cyber security, helpdesk, backup and device management across both schools and the nursery. Estates Management Services - Strategic and operational facilities and estates management, statutory compliance, estates/asset/carbon strategy and H&S support. Communications, Marketing & PR - Brand and reputation management, media and PR, website and social media, prospectus and admissions materials, internal communications. Governance Support Services - Company secretarial and governance support, clerking and minutes (Convene), statutory filings and governance advice. Managed Procurement Services - Procurement advice, tendering and quotations, contracts register, supplier management and Procurement Act 2023 compliance. The full Specification, including service-level agreements, key performance indicators and technical standards for each area, is available to download via the Delta eSourcing website. This procurement is being conducted under the Open Procedure pursuant to section 20(2)(a) of the Act — a single-stage procedure with no restriction on who may submit a tender and no separate shortlisting stage. All compliant tenders received by the deadline will be assessed against the Conditions of Participation, the exclusion grounds and the award criteria in this ITT, and the Contract will be awarded to the Most Advantageous Tender under section 19 of the Act. The deadline for the submission of tenders via the Delta eSourcing portal is 12noon 7 October 2026 For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-Manchester:-Financial-consultancy-services./X7SY8A5TKF To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/X7SY8A5TKF

title: Provision of an eSourcing and Contract Management system via CSS RM1557.14 G-Cloud Framework (Lot 2: Cloud Software)
description: Southend-on-Sea City Council (the "Buyer") currently has in place two separate solutions/contracts for providing an eSourcing procurement and a contract management system. Both contracts are due to expire on 30th November 2026, the current contract for eSourcing system may be further extended to continue to run alongside the contract for the new system to allow the completion of existing procurements to be finalised. The Buyer is now seeking a single provider (the "Supplier") to provide a securely hosted online system which will combine both the management of the full life cycle for both its procurement (eSourcing) and contract management processes. The eSourcing solution will provide a procurement process tool to manage the end-to-end process cycle covering all stages of the tendering process from notice creation to award of contract, including the automated publication of all notices, expressions of interest, requests for information and request for quotes, the secure exchange of all tender documents, a secure messaging system including assessment (evaluation) of bids received. The procurement tool (eSourcing solution) will also capture pre- and post-procurement activity. In addition, it will also provide a contract management tool (contract management solution) to manage the full life cycle of the awarded contract.

title: High-Throughput Experimentation (HTE) Software for Drug Discovery
description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.

title: 390_27 Document Management Solutions
description: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders is 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 12 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

Customers will assess the suppliers as set out in the terms and conditions of the Framework. Please note that once this Framework is established, the right is reserved by the Customer when running a further competitive selection process, to invite the Suppliers to participate in an eAuction. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details.

title: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS
description: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS All central government departments and UK public sector bodies can access open banking related tools and services. Description Instead of relying on card payments, open banking services provide citizens and businesses with an alternative method of paying and/or receiving money from the public sector. You will be able to access a range of open banking services including: payment initiation service providers (PISPs): let you pay companies directly from your bank account rather than using your debit or credit card through a third party, such as Visa or Mastercard account information service providers (AISPs): being an authorised AISP means that a company can access an individual’s bank account data from their financial institution with their explicit consent To help you find the services and suppliers to meet your needs you will be able to use the following filters: service type total contract value hosting and delivery capabilities This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will run for 8 years. Benefits open banking will reduce customer transaction costs where card payments are the existing and only method of payment payments can be made directly from bank account to bank account without the need to repeatedly input details existing customers of the Payment Acceptance framework can transition to Open Banking includes real time bank account data to confirm payee account details reducing the risk of error payments and minimising losses due to fraud Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS Expires: 07/12/2031 How to buy You can access the Open Banking DPS through the Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace. you will need to select the ‘financial services’ section, and scroll to ‘Open Banking’ Select the ‘access as a buyer’ link. you will then be asked to either sign into your Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace account or register for one Accept the terms and conditions of the DPS as a buyer. You can then view and manage your ‘DPS category exports’ page where you will have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export (this is how you filter the suppliers to find those that can meet your needs) When creating a new category use the filtering tool to specify your needs and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘save category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From the ‘manage your category exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (the export is to an Excel spreadsheet). Close the DPS. Use your supplier shortlist to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers in your shortlist to bid against your detailed statement of requirements, evaluation criteria and contract format. Your supplier list is valid for 2 working days from the date of creation. If you do not use your list within 2 working days you will need to create a new supplier list (follow steps 6 to 10). You can use our eSourcing tool to run a competition or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. read guidance for our eSourcing tool Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your needs. You should allow enough time for suppliers to review, prepare a response and ask clarification questions. Evaluate supplier responses. Award the contract. Put a notification of the award on Contracts Finder. Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. title: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit
description: The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) will be for NHS-funded care in England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Jersey (inclusion of other devolved nations/Crown dependencies is yet to be determined and will be detailed within the tender documentation). The initial contract is anticipated to be for a period of 3 years, at a maximum total budget of up to £ 951,168.00 excl VAT and £1,141,401.00 with VAT. Bids exceeding this limit will be rejected. Due to the unknowns in advance of holding the premarket engagement session, it is currently expected that the extension value will be a 2-year pro rata of the core 3-year funding, estimated at £634,112.00 excluding VAT. There is potential to include other Devolved Nations and/or Crown Dependencies, and aspirational measures (which will be defined in the service specification). The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare improvement through the provision of timely and high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data can also improve the system, and there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. The National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) was established in 2011 and has been delivered by the Royal College of Anaesthetists (RCoA) - https://www.nela.org.uk/ The overarching aim of this audit is to stimulate improvements in care for patients undergoing and not undergoing emergency laparotomy through the provision of high-quality comparative data from all providers of emergency laparotomy by measuring and reporting variations in quality of care and patient outcomes. During this contract period, the successful tenderer will need to build on the achievements of the audit to date and enhance the ability for the audit to be used for healthcare improvement by engaging with clinicians, patients and commissioners (both local and national) and regional networks. Successful national audits are those where the individuals providing the data are also in a position to improve the system, and where there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like. Data is most useful locally for healthcare improvement when its provision to clinical teams is timely, the data is refreshed regularly, and appropriate tools, support and guidance accompany the data outputs. The intent is for all of these features to be implemented and improved during the period of this future contract. Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality metrics likely to best support local and national quality improvement Detect, describe and help reduce unwarranted clinical variation by systematically benchmarking performance, identifying outliers, and supporting services to understand variation in outcomes, processes and experience Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate Enable healthcare quality improvements through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named Trust or Health Board, Integrated Care System (ICS), multi-disciplinary team, possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting Engage patients, carers and the public in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit Consider the value and feasibility of linking data at an individual patient level to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future, and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the reports and other audit outputs, and plan and tailor them accordingly. By way of example, the current contract specification includes the following anticipated benefits of the National Emergency Laparotomy Audit: National benchmarking to highlight unwarranted variation between providers Sustained reduction in 30-day mortality and postoperative complications through systematic performance monitoring against national standards Reduced length of hospital stay, supporting faster recovery and improved patient flow Increased delivery of time-critical interventions (e.g. antibiotics for sepsis, timely access to theatre), improving survival and outcomes Enhanced care for high-risk and frail patients, including improved peri-operative specialist input Shift from retrospective reporting to near real-time data and interactive dashboards Improved insight for regulators, commissioners and systems (ICSs) through consistent performance data Systematic identification and management of outliers and ‘cause for concern’, enabling early intervention Standardised performance metrics aligned with NICE and other national guidance Provide audit results in a timely, accessible and meaningful manner to support healthcare quality improvement, minimising the reporting delay and providing continual access to each unit for their own data Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups to drive improvements in services Embedded healthcare improvement plans with measurable objectives and ongoing impact evaluation Support for coordinated improvement across the entire emergency laparotomy pathway Increased use of routine data and data linkage to reduce manual data collection burden Improved data completeness, quality and efficiency, supporting robust analysis and decision-making Systematic assessment of inequalities in access, care and outcomes Support for national and local priorities to reduce inequalities and promote parity of care Active involvement of patients, carers and the public in audit design, outputs and improvement priorities Flexibility to expand scope (e.g. non-operative pathways, wider geographies including devolved nations and Crown Dependencies) Designed to evolve with emerging evidence and service models Further details of the existing audit can be found at: https://www.nela.org.uk/ For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Health-services./C3R5JP672N To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/C3R5JP672N Lot 1: . external_ids: buyer-ref:the association of north east councils limited (nepo):NEPO219
title: NEPO219 - Building Materials & Managed Stores
description: The Association of North East Councils Trading as the North East Procurement Organisation (NEPO) is seeking to establish a multi-supplier, multi-lot Framework for Building Materials and Managed Stores. NEPO intends to publish an Invitation to Tender via the Open eTendering system. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this Framework Agreement must register their expression of interest and submit a tender through the NEPO eTendering system. If not already registered, candidates should register on the Open eTender system at: https://open-uk.org/ Tenders must be submitted using the link above. Tenders submitted via post or email methods will not be accepted. Guidance for how to create an account, search for opportunities and respond is included within the Supplier's hub. If you require further support please email open.support@nepo.org Lot 1: Integrated Materials Management Solutions and Managed Stores. Lot 1 covers the provision of integrated materials management solutions, managed stores, and associated materials management services to support the operational requirements of Contracting Authorities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to integrated materials management solutions and managed stores environments that improve the availability, control and distribution of materials, products and consumables required to support responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management and construction activities. The primary service available under this Lot is an Integrated Materials Management Solution designed to support the efficient sourcing, control, distribution and management of materials, products and consumables. Suppliers shall be capable of delivering integrated materials management solutions designed to provide Contracting Authorities with efficient access to the materials, products and consumables required to support service delivery through one or more coordinated supply channels. Such solutions may incorporate multiple supply chain partners, manufacturers, merchants, distributors and specialist providers operating through a coordinated stores environment or other integrated materials management solution. Integrated materials management solutions may include: Consolidated materials supply arrangements; Multi-source inventory management; Coordinated replenishment services; Centralised issue and distribution points; Integrated ordering solutions; Supply chain coordination; Data analytics and management reporting; Consolidated reporting arrangements; and Demand planning and forecasting The Supplier may deliver these services independently or in collaboration with manufacturers, merchants, distributors, specialist providers or other supply chain organisations. Such arrangements may include the coordination of multiple merchants and specialist suppliers operating through a single managed store or integrated materials management solution where this provides operational or commercial benefit to the Contracting Authority. Integrated materials management solutions and managed stores solutions may be delivered from Contracting Authority premises, Supplier premises or other agreed locations and may include permanent, temporary or mobile facilities. The services available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Managed stores operations; Customer-site stores; Merchant counter solutions; Satellite stores; Mobile and temporary stores; Inventory management services; Materials management services; Stock replenishment services; Vendor managed inventory solutions; Consignment stock arrangements; Van stock management services; Automated dispensing and vending solutions; Supply chain management services; Product standardisation and rationalisation; Electronic ordering and materials management platforms; Digital materials management solutions; Technical support services; and Management information and reporting services. Lot 2: General Materials. Lot 2 covers the supply of general building, construction, maintenance and repair materials to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects, highways maintenance and civil engineering activities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of building materials and associated products required for the construction, maintenance, repair, refurbishment and improvement of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets, together with highways, civil engineering and infrastructure projects. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Building materials; Bricks, blocks and masonry products; Cement, aggregates and associated products; Concrete and precast products; Timber and timber products; Sheet materials; Roofing materials and accessories; Insulation products; Drylining systems; Plaster and plasterboard products; Drainage products; Landscaping materials; Fencing products; Highways and civil engineering materials; Kerbs, channels, paving and block products, including alternative material products (e.g. rubber); Street works and infrastructure materials; Ducting and utility protection products Doors, windows and joinery products; Ironmongery and architectural hardware; Fixings, fasteners and adhesives; Sealants and building chemicals; Decorating materials; Hand tools; Workwear and personal protective equipment (PPE); Site safety products; Construction consumables; and Associated accessories and ancillary products. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of maintenance, construction, highways, public realm, infrastructure and asset improvement projects. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, recycled, low-carbon or environmentally preferable alternatives to standard products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental and net zero objectives. Lot 3: Plumbing, Heating, Gas & Building Services. Lot 3 covers the supply of plumbing, heating, gas, water management and building services products to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects and mechanical building services installations. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of domestic and commercial plumbing, heating and mechanical building services products required for the maintenance, repair, refurbishment, improvement and construction of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Plumbing materials and components; Domestic and commercial heating products; Gas spares and associated equipment; Boilers and water heating systems; Heat pumps and renewable heating technologies; Cylinders and hot water storage solutions; Pumps and pumping equipment; Valves and flow control products; Pipework, fittings and associated accessories; Heating controls and building controls; Thermostats and smart heating systems; Radiators and emitters; Bathrooms and washroom products; Water management and water treatment products; Commercial plant room equipment; Metering and monitoring equipment; Mechanical building services products; Ventilation products associated with heating and plumbing installations; Maintenance, repair and replacement components; Fixings, consumables and ancillary products; and Associated accessories and ancillary items. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of domestic, commercial and public sector maintenance, refurbishment, decarbonisation, compliance and construction projects. This Lot is intended to support both traditional heating and plumbing requirements and the transition to low-carbon technologies. Suppliers should therefore be capable of providing energy-efficient, low-carbon and renewable heating solutions where available, together with associated system components and technical support. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, recycled, low-carbon or environmentally preferable alternatives to standard products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental, decarbonisation and net zero objectives. Lot 4: Electrical. Lot 4 covers the supply of electrical products, components and associated accessories to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects and electrical installations. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of electrical products required for the maintenance, repair, refurbishment, improvement and construction of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Electrical cables and wiring products; Cable management and containment systems; Distribution equipment and switchgear; Circuit protection devices; Consumer units and distribution boards; Wiring accessories; Lighting products and associated controls; Emergency lighting systems; Lamps and luminaires; Fire detection and alarm products; Security and access control products; CCTV and surveillance equipment; Data, communications and network infrastructure products; Testing and monitoring equipment; Metering and energy management products; Batteries and power supplies; Electric vehicle charging infrastructure and associated components; Renewable energy electrical components; Electrical maintenance, repair and replacement components; Fixings, consumables and ancillary products; and Associated accessories and ancillary items. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of domestic, commercial and public sector maintenance, refurbishment, compliance, decarbonisation and construction projects. This Lot is intended to support both traditional electrical installations and emerging technologies. Suppliers should therefore be capable of providing energy-efficient and low-carbon solutions where available, including products which support electrification, renewable energy generation, energy management and electric vehicle infrastructure. description: This service provides a comprehensive, Microsoft 365 - native data governance solution designed to improve information security, compliance and lifecycle management across YPO's digital estate. The service supports automated or workflow-based sensitivity labelling, robust exception handling, and safe, controlled remediation with rollback capabilities. It identifies ROT and stale data, enabling defensible disposition aligned with retention policies. Continuous monitoring highlights external sharing risks, permission drift, and newly created unlabelled content. Real-time dashboards, exportable reports, and ISO27001 - ready evidence packs support audit readiness and operational oversight. The solution operates fully within YPO Microsoft 365 tenant, ensuring no data exfiltration, strong security controls, and full alignment with GDPR and organisational compliance requirements.

title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning
description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.

description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. title: CivTech 11 - Challenge 11.6 - How can technology reduce teacher workload?
description: The workload, expectations and demands on teachers has increased. While we can pinpoint different factors contributing to increasing workloads, we don’t know enough about how these manifest themselves for teachers, nor how they vary at different career stages, in different school contexts (high school, primary etc) or across different roles (principal teacher, department head, management etc). This Challenge seeks to reduce teacher workload by developing a strong understanding of the reality of teachers’ different, varying experiences and so drive the development of products that teachers (and related professions) want to use and make a real impact on reducing workload. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Digital Directorate, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are.. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-11 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-11-challenge-6-reducing-teaching-workload

title: Design Consultancy Framework
description: Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust is procuring a four-year, multi-supplier Estates Design and Construction Consultancy Framework to support its capital and estates programmes. The framework will cover 11 specialist consultancy Lots, including design, engineering, project management, surveying and contract administration services. The procurement will use a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure, comprising an SQ followed by an ITT, with up to three suppliers appointed per Lot Lot 1: Full Design Services. Provision of multidisciplinary design consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include architectural, structural, civil, mechanical, electrical and public health design, together with coordination of specialist disciplines and overall design management. The Lot is intended to provide an integrated design service from a single consultancy or multidisciplinary team across projects of varying scale and complexity Lot 10: Authorising Engineers. Provision of Authorising Engineer consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include independent technical advice, compliance assurance, audits and assessments, review of engineering systems and procedures, appointment and assessment of Authorised Persons, and specialist guidance to support the safe operation and management of healthcare engineering systems. Lot 11: Quantity Surveying and Contract Administration Services. Provision of quantity surveying and contract administration consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include cost planning, estimating, procurement and tender support, contract administration, valuations, change control, cost reporting, final accounts and commercial advice throughout the design, construction and completion stages of projects. Lot 2: Principal Designer Services. Provision of Principal Designer services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme, including management and coordination of health and safety considerations during the design phase. Services may include supporting compliance with relevant CDM and Building Regulations requirements, coordinating designers, identifying and managing design-related risks, and providing appropriate advice and assurance throughout the design and construction process Lot 3: Architectural Services. Provision of architectural design and consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include feasibility studies, concept and detailed design, planning support, design development, technical specifications and coordination with other design disciplines across healthcare refurbishment, redevelopment and new-build projects. Lot 4: Civil and Structural Engineering Services. Provision of civil and structural engineering consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include structural assessments, surveys, feasibility studies, structural and civil design, drainage and infrastructure design, technical specifications and coordination with other design disciplines across refurbishment, redevelopment and new-build projects. Lot 5: Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing Services. Provision of mechanical, electrical and plumbing engineering consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include surveys, feasibility studies, system assessments, design and specification of building services, energy and sustainability solutions, infrastructure upgrades and coordination with other design disciplines across refurbishment, redevelopment and new-build projects. Lot 6: Fire Engineering Services. Provision of fire engineering consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include fire safety design and strategy, technical assessments, fire engineering advice, review of design proposals, support with regulatory compliance and coordination with other design disciplines across refurbishment, redevelopment and new-build healthcare projects. Lot 7: Project Management. Provision of project management consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include project planning, programme and risk management, stakeholder coordination, governance and reporting, procurement support, cost and programme monitoring, and management of projects from inception through design, construction, commissioning and completion. Lot 8: Building Surveying Services. Provision of building surveying consultancy services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include building condition surveys, defect diagnosis, feasibility studies, refurbishment advice, preparation of specifications and schedules of work, compliance assessments and technical advice relating to the maintenance, improvement and development of the Trust’s estate Lot 9: Clerk of Works Services. Provision of Clerk of Works services to support the Trust’s capital and estates programme. Services may include site inspections, monitoring workmanship and materials, checking compliance with drawings and specifications, identifying defects and quality issues, maintaining inspection records, reporting on construction progress and supporting the Trust in achieving required quality standards throughout project delivery.
framework: The Framework will operate as a closed, multi-supplier framework for a period of four years. Call-off contracts may be awarded through Direct Award or Mini-Competition, depending on the value, complexity and requirements of the commission. Supplier selection will consider relevant experience, performance, capability, resource availability, specialist expertise and value for money. Prices will be based on the framework rates agreed at award or determined through project-specific commercial proposals or Mini-Competitions, as appropriate.

title: External Audit
description: 1.1. Loreburn Housing Association (LHA), a Registered Social Landlord, is looking for a firm of registered Auditors to carry out its External Audit services for a period of three years from Financial Years 2026/30 onwards, with a potential to extend this for a further 2 years. 1.2. The External Audit service will provide the LHA Management Committee with an independent and objective opinion on the financial statements in accordance with the relevant legal and regulatory requirements and International Standards of Auditing. The audit will also provide the Management Committee with a view on internal controls, governance arrangements, and risk management by measuring and evaluating their effectiveness in supporting LHA’s corporate objectives. In addition, the successful Auditor may be engaged from time to time by LHA to perform ad hoc assignments. 1.3. The external audit firm may also be invited to provide certain management consultancy services as agreed. Applicable daily rates for specialist consultancy staff should be provided. To avoid potential conflicts of interest, the Association wishes to specifically exclude the successful external audit firm from undertaking certain consultancy assignments on their behalf, for example internal audit. 1.4. LHA forms part of the Loreburn Group. There is one associated company of LHA – Dumfries and Galloway Home Limited (DGH) – SC304439. The board of this company also requires the services of a firm of registered Auditors to carry out its External Audit services and Corporate Tax services for a period of three years from Financial Years 2025/26 onwards, with a potential to extend this for a further 2 years and this also forms part of this tender. It is envisaged that the same firm of Auditors will act for both entities. Lot 1: . 3.1.6. The external audit and tax service will include, but not be limited to: - The planning, management, and efficient execution of the annual external audit of financial statements - Preparation of an annual audit plan for each business to be made available to each board in line with the timetable below - Formal reporting to the Audit and Compliance committee, the Management Committee, and any other Board meetings where the members require clarification of the accounts. - Meetings with the Executive management team pre and post audit to discuss audit plan and audit report respectively in advance of Committee/Board meetings - Review of the final financial statements on behalf of the group companies for accuracy, in terms of technical and numerical. The draft accounts will be prepared by the LHA Group Head of Finance. - The Auditor will prepare an annual audit finding report for the financial year for presentation at a meeting of the Audit & Compliance Committee on completion of their audit by the agreed dates in the table below - The report will include; - Summary of activity against plan. - Main recommendations, responses and outcomes. - Limitations on audit. - Overall assessment of internal controls. - Recommendations for changes, improvements, etc. to the External Audit Service, with costings if necessary. - Audit field work on site for up to 5 days for the final audit. Regular progress updates to management to be provided during the field work, concluding with a clearance meeting encompassing all audit issues. Therefore, all works must be based on a total of 10 days for the pricing schedule. - Attendance at LHA’s Annual General Meeting with a report presentation - Provision of timely and accurate advice and guidance on technical accounting and finance issues. Owing to the time critical nature of the process of preparation of annual financial statements it is expected that the principal external audit contacts will be readily available by telephone/email and will provide a full response to requests within 2 working days. - Preparation and submission of the Corporation Tax Return for DGH. - Timely provision of relevant technical accounting updates, including relevant Financial Reporting Standards, Statements of Recommended Practice and Accounting Orders. - Excellent and timely communication between auditor and client on all matters, including feedback on information supplied and immediate feedback on any predicted cost over-runs. - The provision of added value and innovation to the audit process. - The supplier is expected to use their skill, knowledge and expertise to identify any gaps in this scope and address them in their submission. - Co-operation with LHA’s internal auditors where you wish to rely on their assurance work when planning the statutory audit. (This service is being tendered at the same time to separate organisation in line with our Financial Regulations) - Submission of accounts to company’s house for DGH. 3.1.7. In addition, we may require the external auditor to provide expert professional advice and guidance on: - Corporation Tax issues affecting the Association and the Subsidiary. - VAT issues. - Other relevant taxation issues, for example, PAYE/NI, Capital Gains Tax etc.
