The response presents no risks or concerns to the overall service delivery. Responses will be individually assessed according to the scoring system above. title: Data of Last Resort Data Collection
description: This Market Engagement seeks to identify options to enable procurement of a dedicated backup collection tool for Operational Technology (OT) environments. The solution will ensure that the complete data state of critical OT assets is consistently captured and securely stored across multiple sites, serving as the organisation's data of last resort. The tool must collect the full backup state of OT assets including configurations, control logic, firmware, hardware metadata, and associated files. It must support both automated, policy-driven backup collection and authorised manual backup initiation, operating through secure and non-intrusive protocols that do not interact with OT control or programming interfaces and have no impact on live operations or safety-critical systems. The solution must be vendor-agnostic, deployable fully on-premise or within a private cloud, and capable of operating in air-gapped environments, with full audit trails and compliance reporting. IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. title: PME Erasmus
description: This is not a call for competition. The London Borough of Croydon is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to the potential commissioning of an Erasmus+ teacher/educator training and international mobility programme for Croydon schools. The Council is seeking expressions of interest only from organisations with demonstrable previous experience of managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects and international education mobility programmes on behalf of schools or public-sector organisations. The appointed provider would be expected to provide end-to-end programme management, including: • Previous experience of successfully managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects, including details of the number and type of projects delivered • Management and coordination of international teacher training, CPD and school visits across European destinations, with destinations to be confirmed • Organisation and management of participant travel, accommodation, and associated logistics • Support with participant recruitment and selection, including ensuring appropriate eligibility and allocation processes • Management of Erasmus+ grant administration, financial monitoring, evidence, and reporting requirements • Support for safeguarding, risk management and participant welfare throughout the programme • Delivery or commissioning of high-quality teacher CPD and training aligned to the agreed programme objectives • Development and implementation of programme evaluation, impact measurement, and outcomes reporting • Monitoring and reporting on participant outcomes and the wider impact of the programme on participating schools; and • Effective stakeholder management and communication with the Council, schools, training providers, and international partners. The programme is intended to support Croydon schools in developing practice in areas including inclusion and SEND, digital and AI-enabled education, wellbeing, sustainability, innovation, and oracy/communication-rich learning, aligned with relevant Erasmus+ priorities. Providers should only register an interest where they can demonstrate the relevant specialist experience, capacity, international networks and organisational infrastructure required to manage an Erasmus+ mobility programme from participant selection through to final evaluation and grant reporting. Registering your interest Providers wishing to participate must register their interest through the correspondence area no later than 21 September 2026 Please complete the sections provided in the document attached and return via the messaging area on the inTend Portal: Following the registration deadline, the Council will review responses and may engage with organisations whose experience and capabilities align with the requirements. This market engagement exercise is intended to inform the Council's understanding of the market and potential future commissioning arrangements. It does not constitute a procurement process, and participation does not provide any advantage in any future procurement activity. Organisation name Main contact name and job title Contact email address A brief response confirming: • the number of Erasmus+ projects your organisation has previously managed • your experience of managing international school/teacher mobility programmes • your experience of grant administration and reporting • your ability to manage travel, accommodation, participant selection, safeguarding, CPD and evaluation; and • a brief example of a comparable programme successfully delivered. Word Limit: 250 words The London Borough of Croydon use the Intend portal to manage supplier records and to run procurement activities. If you do not yet have an account, please register, if you do have an account, It is essential that your company information on Intend matches the details held by Companies House, please do log in and check this. Intend Portal: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/croydontenders/aspx/Home Register on the Central Digital Platform If you haven’t already, please register your organisation on the Central Digital Platform. This is a government-wide initiative to streamline supplier engagement and improve transparency. Again please do ensure your information matches your Companies House details. Central Digital Platform Registration: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/suppliers-how-to-register-your-organisation-and-first-administrator-on-find-a-tender-in-three-easy-steps-html We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to working together. Introduction This document is issued as part of a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise by The London Fire Commissioner. better known as the London Fire Brigade (LFB). This is a specialised training which can only be carried out in specific secure training environments with smoke rooms and specialist buildings designed and built to be used to train officers to respond in smoke filled environments. Information gathered through this engagement will assist the Authority in understanding market capability, refining its requirements, and determining the most appropriate procurement strategy. 3. title: Dietary Surveys and Analysis
description: AWARD OF CONTRACT - Food Standards Scotland (FSS) is the public sector food body for Scotland. Our vision is a food and drink environment that benefits, protects and is trusted by consumers. We are here to make sure that food is safe to eat, ensure consumers know what they are eating, and improve the extent to which they have diets that are conducive to good health. The Nutrition Programme includes a dietary surveillance work stream to monitor and report progress towards the Scottish Dietary Goals (SDGs). FSS are looking to award a contract to a provider who can conduct dietary surveys and analysis over a period of three (3) years with the option to extend up to a further 24 months. Lot 1: . AWARD OF CONTRACT - FSS's primary method for assessing dietary intake in Scotland is via an online, multiple pass dietary assessment method known as Intake24, which has been used to collect data as part of the Scottish Health Survey (SHeS) since 2021. This provides FSS with robust dietary intake data in a representative sample of the Scottish population, linked with demographic and health data collected in the main SHeS survey allowing us to monitor progress towards the SDGs. Although representative of the whole of Scotland, SHeS does not allow FSS to take a close look at the dietary intake of smaller groups of interest e.g. minority groups. Conducting additional surveys in specific population groups in Scotland, using Intake24, would allow FSS to further investigate dietary intakes in these groups. The provider will complete a range of projects in the field of surveys and analysis, including but not limited to: - Designing, conducting and analysing a survey on ethnic minority groups in Scotland using Intake24. - Conducting analysis on retail and out of home purchase of food and drink in Scotland. - Research considering the wider environmental impact diet has on food systems. - Research incorporating qualitative measures to provide a mixed methods approach building on quantitative research. - To conduct literature reviews as required by FSS.

title: Child Poverty Action Plan - Programme Evaluation
description: The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030. The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions. The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan. The programme‐level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme. title: P12819 - National School of Government and Public Services
description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. Market Involvement As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers. With this in mind, Cabinet Office and the project team have planned the following Sector Connector events. title: MyMCA UK Maritime Services Portal Development
description: This procurement will enable the MCA to carry out a discovery and alpha exercise to explore how Ship Owners/Operators and Third-Party Ship Personnel and Management Organisations carry out their business through the MyMCA Platform. To date, the concept of MyMCA has addressed the user needs for Seafarers and how they apply for their Certificate of Competency (CoC) as well as how Short Course Providers and MCA Approved doctors integrate with MyMCA as part of that process. This new work will explore how Ship Owners/Operators and Third-Party Ship/Personnel Management Organisations will carry out their business and may include processes such as survey booking/scheduling, viewing and managing ship/other certificates and online payment for services. During discovery work, detailed user research will be carried out to understand the pain points for customers (as well as internal users) as well as identifying manual process that can be brought online for the benefits of MCA and the customers. "As is" and "To Be" user journeys will be mapped to support iterative prototype developments which will be tested with users during the subsequent alpha phase. These journeys/prototypes will then be subject to GDS assessments before its rolled into the MyMCA platform during beta. Stage 1 of the DOS 5 process was concluded via CAS on the 25/08/23 therefore this project captures Stage 2 of the process to be undertaken via online e-procurement services.

description: The Senior Data Scientist will support the transformation and modernisation of organisational data analytics capabilities in support of the organisation's Data Strategy and Public Sector Reform ambitions. title: Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services
description: Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) that will help to maximise public sector services and support the UK National Space Strategy and Geospatial strategy. This agreement has suppliers that can provide remote geospatial, locational, communication and sensing capabilities. Services available may include data, technology solutions and aerial and land-based platforms. Updates 19 May 2025: This framework agreement will expire 10 February 2029. It will now run alongside RM6370 Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market, which will go live August 2025. Description Provides a simple and efficient route to a wide range of competition in a new market. We developed this agreement to support: UK national space strategy Geospatial strategy Products and services available under this agreement provide a broad scope for the space enabled technology market, including the geospatial ecosystem. Geospatial ecosystem refers to any solution using data about location, or ‘geospatial’ data. This data tells us where people and objects are in relation to a particular geographic location, whether in the air, on the ground, at sea or under our feet. Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services provides you with the opportunity to access almost any relevant and commercially available product or service in this area, including ‘off the shelf’ services and ‘bespoke’ services. Bespoke services will allow you to make changes to a product or service so that it better meets your individual needs. Available products and services include: data products, such as aerial photography or services to monitor demographic changes over time and may include: using existing data sets creating bespoke surveys designed to meet the specific needs of your estate or service ongoing monitoring services remote sensing or monitoring services which allows continuous or specific collection of data, including satellite or unmanned autonomous vehicles (UAVs) and drone platforms UAV platform products, such as drones or counter drone technology, that may operate in the air, on land, or in water and be able to monitor, photograph or transport items process and workforce transformation solutions: to improve workflow by reducing the need to manually monitor physical data (such as size, temperature or composition) over long distances or time periods for example, using a satellite earth-observation service to monitor for tree disease across forests broadcast or communications enabled by satellite technology, including broadband internet or voice communication devices or services professional services such as service design, operations support, training or other consultancy services related to any part of the wider scope this includes professional services relating to space launch or manufacture for space (referred to as ‘upstream’) digital applications or services that make use of geospatial data to create interactive maps or databases, you can use these applications to link to and regularly update your organisation’s existing systems Benefits access to a previously under-used market allows for better decision making by supporting the public sector to either improve the way existing services are provided or to discover the value of existing locational data our solutions can help you do this by monitoring, collecting or analysing geospatial data and trends considers the safety, efficiency or environmental benefits of remote monitoring and sensing from satellite, UAV or other technologies provides a route to market for buying satellite enabled communication and broadcasting in hard to reach locations such as remote train stations or disaster-hit areas, where traditional land-based communication methods or mobile networks aren’t as effective as a DPS the agreement will continue to onboard new suppliers including SMEs throughout the lifecycle, providing access to a range of suppliers and broad competition we have designed the broad scope to reduce restrictive definitions, leaving the agreement open to innovative and emerging capabilities we expect this growing market to introduce new solutions of value to the public sector over the course of the agreement’s lifetime supports social value guidance issued under PPN 06/20 and carbon reduction guidance issued under PPN 06/21 designed to support and complement the government’s Geospatial Strategy Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services We have organised services using filters to help you select capable suppliers who can meet your needs, these filters are: Category of requirement: allows you to specify whether your need is relevant to: satellite communications geospatial data and services UAV solutions upstream professional services Service or product to be provided allows you to define the broad type of product or service(s) that you will need from the supplier to fulfil your needs Specialist capabilities provides an opportunity to reduce your supplier shortlist further based on particular sets of capabilities that the supplier should have Commercial model capability allows you to identify whether you would prefer a traditional ‘project or milestone based’ approach or an ‘X or (‘anything’) as a service’ approach. Expires: 10/02/2029 How to buy Before using this agreement you should read the customer guidance document. This document will provide you with a better understanding of the further competition process. We have organised this DPS into 4 categories: category of requirement service or products to be provided specialist capabilities commercial model capability To select a supplier, you must run a mini competition. There is no option for direct award. Before you run your mini competition, you will need to find out which suppliers can meet your needs using the DPS marketplace . The DPS marketplace will allow you to shortlist suppliers using a number of filters which covers the capabilities of the suppliers and what they can offer. Once you have created your supplier shortlist you will then need to run a further competition. You will need to invite all your shortlisted suppliers to take part. The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition: Register on the Supplier Registration Service. Go to the DPS page for Space-Enabled and Geospatial Services by scrolling down the DPS Marketplace landing page. Select ‘space-enabled and Geospatial services’ and access by agreeing to the terms of use. Use the filters to select your needs and filter appropriate suppliers. Use Annex 1 of the customer guidance document. Export your list of DPS suppliers and contact details by clicking the ‘export supplier list’ link. we recommend that you use your exported supplier list within 2 working days as new suppliers may apply to join at any point, and this will change who is eligible to compete in a further competition Create a competition on the customer’s chosen eProcurement or tendering system. Invite the identified DPS suppliers and provide your: specification evaluation criteria contract format To run your further competition, you can use our free eSourcing tool. Run your competition and evaluate supplier responses. allow at least 10 days for supplier(s) to respond for standard projects and, where a project is more complex, you should consider allowing more time Ask the winning supplier(s) to provide any needed evidence to show that they can meet your needs. Supplier(s) will share this evidence through the DPS marketplace platform. we recommend that you do this within 2 days for non-complex projects, more complex projects will allow for more time Once you are satisfied with the evidence, proceed to award. Inform us of contract award using theRM6235 DPS. Issue contract award notice on Contracts Finder. Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. Documents published before this date may still refer to CCS. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. title: Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework
description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. Services required: • Transport of materials and equipment within the Lake District National Park using helicopters • Airlift operations • Load preparation (stropping, bunding) • Ground crew provision • Flight planning and risk assessment Lot 8: Higher Value Practical Works - £50,000 and over. The Authority secures frequent bids for grant money provided by national, regional and local government as well as charitable organisations and private funding organisations. This funding enables the Authority to undertake larger scale and usually multi-facetted projects or programmes of work varying in value from the high tens of thousands of pounds to the low millions of pounds. Such projects may involve delivery of one type of product or service across a range of sites throughout the park or a multi-facetted project including access, nature conservation, interpretation, and conservation of the heritage-built environment. We are looking for suppliers who can provide work at scale and across a range of areas, either directly or by acting as Primary Contractors and providing project management and delivering work through co-ordinating multiple suppliers and contractors. Examples of such work packages include the establishment of the Coast-to-Coast National Trail, barn restoration through the Farming in Protected Landscapes programme and Access for All projects. The type of work is similar to that contained in Lots 1, 2, and 3 but at large scale. Services required: • General construction project work (see description) • Sub soiling • Stone flags • Pitching • Construction Design and Management work • Supply and construction of bridges • Public path works • Securing relevant consents, assents and planning permissions • Woodland Management • Grassland restoration • Riverbank Stabilization
framework: Framework maximum prices are determined at the point of tendering and evaluation, subject to an annual increase in accordance with the Consumer Prices Index. Price Scoring Methodology Price evaluation will be conducted as follows: • The lowest price submission for that Lot, or Item in the case of Lots 1 and 2, will be allocated the highest score (5) and the highest price the lowest score (1). • The prices falling in between the highest and lowest price for that Lot or Item will be scored based on the percentage difference between the lowest price and the highest price. • For Lots 1 and 2 each item will be scored individually, and an overall average score for the Lot will be calculated based on the number of items that have been priced for by each tenderer. Direct award and further competition will be available at the point of Call-Off in accordance with the final Framework Agreement terms.

title: Technical Implementation Partner & Business Change Partner (DASP)
description: NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) is procuring delivery partners for the Donor and Session Programme (DASP), a strategic digital transformation programme to modernise donor engagement, appointment booking, session management and related donor-facing and operational capabilities across blood, platelets and plasma. The procurement is divided into two Lots: Lot 1: Technical Implementation Partner The Technical Implementation Partner will support the technical implementation of the selected CRM Platform and associated digital ecosystem. The scope includes solution design, configuration, integration, data migration, testing, deployment, transition, implementation governance, technical assurance and operational readiness. Suppliers tendering for Lot 1 must align their Tender Response to one of the eligible CRM Platforms identified in the Invitation to Tender documents. The proposed technical solution, implementation approach and associated commercial submissions must be prepared consistently on the basis of the selected CRM Platform. Lot 2: Business Change Partner The Business Change Partner will support the business change, adoption and operational transformation required to implement DASP successfully. The scope includes operating model and workforce transformation, stakeholder engagement, change impact assessment, communications, learning and capability development, adoption planning, business readiness, benefits realisation and transition to business as usual. NHSBT intends to award a single-supplier contract for each Lot. Suppliers may tender for either Lot or both Lots but must submit a complete and independently compliant Tender Response for each Lot tendered for. The full requirements, eligible CRM Platforms, procurement procedure, Conditions of Participation, award criteria, evaluation methodology, timetable, contract terms and submission instructions are set out in the Invitation to Tender and associated tender documents available through Atamis under reference C468497. title: Heart Attack Diagnosis Software Development
description: Creation of software application classed as medical device. The University of Edinburgh has developed a novel algorithm which may improve the accuracy of heart-attack diagnosis in the emergency department. A prototype of this software has been developed. The objective of this procurement is to identify a supplier to create a productionised version of this software tool, which for regulatory purposes in the UK, USA and EU would be classified as a ‘Medical Device’. Such a supplier will have exceptional competence in software development, and prior experience in creation of software classed as a ‘Medical Device’. The supplier will be expected to (but not limited to...); Demonstrate their prior expertise via example projects and references Utilise modern, reliable, and maintainable programming language/s, frameworks and components to deliver the project. Operate a quality management system in line with ISO13485 and follow any and all relevant guidance set by medical regulatory bodies in the UK, EU and USA in relation to production of software classed as a ‘medical device’ Utilise test-oriented development and design and deliver a test strategy for the development Operate a sophisticated project management approach and transparent progress reporting and governing to maximise potential success of the project Demonstrate how they will manage risk and uncertainty to ensure the project falls explicitly within the cost appetite Be open to regulatory audit, if required, by a medical regulator in the UK, EU or USA; or, by a third party acting for the University for regulatory outcomes, which may include desktop review or site visit The University anticipates awarding a Master Services Agreement to set the basis of the engagement and an initial engagement Statement of Work for the creation, testing and regulatory approval. The estimated value of the tender represents an initial cost appetite of GBP180k (including VAT) (which the University may review from time to time), with contingency for potential additional work packages over the maximum term of the agreement. The estimate does not reflect an offer or promise of business above any contract which is ultimately signed by the parties. AI Policy; Due to the proprietary nature of the IP in this engagement and the human-safety implications of this technology; A.The supplier at no time will be permitted to expose or query any part of the IP the University provides to the supplier to any public facing/internet connected AI system (including but not limited to ChatGPT, Grok, Claude etc.). Any other automated system is only to be used with permission of the University and with proper transparency about how it operates and is isolated from potential data harvesting or exfiltration. B.The supplier shall not utilise any other AI to automatically generate the code base or any substantial part of it. (i.e. ‘Vibe coding’) C.AI must not be utilised in the core logic, the app must be deterministic D.The supplier shall be required to undertake human code review and resilience checking in addition to any automated tools The complete requirements are set out in the procurement documentation. Award The University anticipates awarding a Master Services Agreement contract with a supplier for software development services for a period of 5 years, and an initial statement of work for the development of the productionised software product and supporting this through regulatory approvals. Variation and options The University reserves the right to award additional work packages to the winning Tenderer via the Negotiated Procedure Without Prior Call for Competition

title: Cheshire and Warrington Growth Hub Business Support Services
description: This ITT sets out the information which is required in order to assess the suitability of bidders in terms of their capacity to deliver flexible, responsive business support, quality assurance processes, relationship management, service levels and innovative solutions to meet the requirements of ECW for Cheshire and Warrington Growth Hub Support Services Across Cheshire and Warrington, businesses have had access to a wide range of support offers. However, this provision is often time limited, programme specific, or fragmented across organisations, which can make navigation difficult for SMEs. Businesses frequently report uncertainty about who does what, leading to disengagement after initial enquiry. The available services have been curtailed recently due to funding reductions. ECW is commissioning a service to address this gap on an interim basis via an embedded service within the existing Cheshire and Warrington Growth Hub. The service should be designed to also add resource to the National Business Growth Service by ensuring businesses receive timely, proportionate, hands on support that helps them take action and progress. The additional service will operate as part of the Growth Hub and is intended to complement, existing provision at a national, regional and local level. The interim provision will include practical delivery, hands on adviser support, follow up, and business readiness -ensuring clear referral pathways, feedback loops, and effective navigation across the ecosystem. ECW wish to secure efficiencies and economies of scale by means of a procurement exercise for meeting the requirements detailed within this documentation. The principle benefits anticipated by ECW in this procurement include; • Ability to maximise opportunities for best value and efficient services • To allow bidders to explore efficiencies, which may be possible by suggesting innovative and cost-effective solutions • Presentation of cost savings to ECW in order to maximise economical operational efficiency and value for money • A resultant contract that meets the tender requirements and supports ECW with their ambition This service would be commissioned on an interim basis for 12 months, with quarterly reviews. This is intended to maintain continuity of business support during the transition to a Cheshire and Warrington Combined Authority-led service, while also establishing a scalable model capable of adapting to future devolved arrangements. During the contract life, the successful bidder will need to achieve continuous improvement against KPIs, customer satisfaction and other contract measures. Failure to do so may result in the contract being terminated.

title: CPT_26_03 IT Service management (ITSM)
description: The National Audit Office (NAO) is the UK's independent public spending watchdog. It supports Parliament in holding government to account and helps improve public services through high quality audit and assurance work. The NAO sought to appoint an experienced supplier to provide an enterprise-grade IT Service Management (ITSM) solution and associated support services for internal users across the organisation. The requirement included the provision, implementation, configuration, and ongoing support of an ITSM platform capable of supporting core ITSM processes, including incident management, service requests, change management, asset and configuration management, workflow automation, reporting, and governance. The solution is required to be scalable, configurable, and proportionate to the NAO's operational needs, and capable of supporting multiple internal functional areas. The procurement sought a supplier capable of delivering a controlled transition from the incumbent system, including secure data migration, integration with the NAO's Microsoft-based digital estate, and service readiness activities, with minimal disruption to business operations. The solution is required to provide an intuitive user experience, configurable workflows, and accessible reporting, without reliance on complex development or ongoing external consultancy. The requirement also included robust ongoing platform support, including routine updates, security maintenance and patching, and effective vulnerability management and remediation. This includes the ability to identify, assess, track, prioritise, and remediate security vulnerabilities affecting the ITSM platform and its components, supported by appropriate controls, governance, and reporting. The successful supplier is required to provide assurance that vulnerabilities are managed in line with recognised industry good practice and the NAO's information security and risk management requirements. In addition, the procurement sought a supplier able to demonstrate a sustainable product roadmap and ongoing service support model to ensure long-term service continuity, platform resilience, and alignment with the NAO's future operational and digital requirements. The contract will commence on Monday 2 November 2026 and includes an initial six-month mobilisation and implementation period, with service go-live anticipated from Tuesday 1 June 2027. The initial contract term is three (3) years until Friday 31 May 2030, with options to extend for up to two further periods of twelve (12) months, up to a maximum contract end date of Monday 31 May 2032. The contract has been awarded with a maximum value of up to £1.8 million inclusive of VAT over the full potential five-year term. Lot 1: . None

title: AMCV 355 - Digital Solutions to Support Unpaid Carers
description: Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action. Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer. Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner. Any proposed solution should offer the following support: Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally. Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions. Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed. Lot 1: . None

description: East Renfrewshire Council is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced organisation to undertake an independent Best Value Review of Enjoy East Ren. The review will evaluate the extent to which Enjoy East Ren delivers best value in line with the definition and themes set out by Audit Scotland and will provide clear, evidence-based recommendations for ongoing improvement. Lot 1: . East Renfrewshire Council is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced organisation to undertake an independent Best Value Review of Enjoy East Ren. The review will evaluate the extent to which Enjoy East Ren delivers best value in line with the definition and themes set out by Audit Scotland and will provide clear, evidence-based recommendations for ongoing improvement. The review should build on previous work, including the 2018 Solace in Business review and the 2020 Best Value review, and should consider the current delivery model, future service requirements, opportunities for improvement and the ongoing relationship between the Council and the Trust. The Council requires the review to be independent, proportionate, practical and capable of supporting future decision-making in relation to leisure, culture, facilities, governance, financial sustainability and community outcomes.
eligibility_text: ISO 9001 or equivalent quality management accrediatation, demonstrating robust arrangements for project delivery, quality assurance, document control, peer review and continuous improvement. To establish the financial standing of a bidder, the Council will: Take into account a risk report provided independently by Creditsafe. Within such reports, the risk of business failure is expressed as a score ranging from 1 -100. In the event that a company is determined to have a risk failure rating of below 30 i.e. that the company is considered to have a high risk of business failure, the submission will not be considered further. Where the score is 30+ the Council will consider all information available from the report. Where you are not registered on credit safe e.g. charitable organisations, new start companies and Sole Traders you are to submit 2 years financial accounts, including Profit & Loss Statement and Balance Sheet for consideration. It should be noted that in addition to the above checks the Council reserves the right at its own discretion to seek such other information from the applicant in accordance with Regulation 61(7) or Regulation 61(8) of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 to determine the applicant’s economic and financial standing. Additional information can include an analysis of turnover, solvency ratios and profitability ratios and will be detailed within the Qualification Envelope question within PCS-Tender. The final decision on bidder inclusion rests with the Council.

Phoenix is a bespoke, business-critical platform used by Rail Staff Travel Limited to manage rail staff travel benefits for approximately one million rail employees, pensioners and eligible family members. Phase 3 will complete the migration of the remaining Phoenix portal functionality, customer-facing processes and core data management capabilities onto the modernised technical architecture established during Phases 1 and 2. The works will improve usability, cyber security, resilience, data integrity and long-term sustainability while enabling the retirement of legacy technology components. The proposed contract is being awarded on the basis that, due to technical dependencies arising from the delivery of the previous phases, only the incumbent supplier can reasonably complete the programme without significant duplication of work, technical rediscovery, delay and increased operational risk Lot 1: . title: GGC0904 Professional Services - Estates Minor Works
description: NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Health Board and Golden Jubilee Hospital (hereafter referred to as ‘The Board’) Estates team regularly appoint a variety of external consultants to undertake scoping, design, tender and construction management activities. The volume of tender exercises currently being undertaken has identified the need for a framework to be established that provides a better value process for procuring Professional Consultancy Services. The Framework Contract will be for a period of up to forty eight (48) months from its commencement date. Overall, the creation of a framework is for the following Lots which will ensure that the procurement process aligns with the public nature and fair procurement values of NHS Scotland. -Lot 1: MEP Engineering Consultancy -Lot 2: Energy Consultancy -Lot 3: CDM Principle Designer -Lot 4: Project Management & Cost Advisers Promotion of transparency, quality, efficiency, compliance, and long-term collaboration, contributing to the delivery of safe, efficient, and cost-effective healthcare facilities. Lot 1: Professional Services Framework - MEP Engineering Consultancy. The appointed MEP Engineering Consultants will provide comprehensive services spanning all RIBA stages, focusing on the design, planning, and management of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems. The consultant will collaborate with clients, principal designers, and other consultants to develop engineering solutions that meet the project’s technical, environmental, and functional requirements. Lot 2: Professional Services Framework - Energy Consultancy. The Energy Consultant shall provide services under the Framework Agreement for commercial projects, adhering to the Contract Documents. The Consultant is expected to deliver high-quality services that offer value for money and to strive for excellence in all aspects of the Consultancy Service. This includes providing services throughout the various RIBA Stages. Lot 3: Estates Professional Services - CDM Principle Designer. The role of a Principal Designer who is required to fully comply under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015 (CDM 2015) and who are crucial in ensuring health and safety throughout the design and planning stages of a construction project. Lot 4: Estates Professional Services - Project Management & Cost Adviser. The Project Manager and Cost Adviser is a key professional role responsible for overseeing the planning, execution, and financial management of construction and infrastructure projects. This role ensures projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. The professional combines project management expertise with cost control and financial planning to provide comprehensive oversight and guidance throughout the project lifecycle.

title: On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability) Franchising and Wider Transport Ticketing & Payment Consultancy Services
description: Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members. The Goods and Services will be supplied via Award Without Competition and by Competitive Selection Process. Lot 1 of this Framework is seeking the provision of On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability). Lot 1 - has 9 parts: Lot 1 - Part 1 - Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) Solution Provision of an integrated Automated Vehicle Location solution capable of accurately determining and communicating vehicle location in real time. The solution shall support route, journey and stop association, estimated arrival/departure information and integration with other onboard and back-office systems. Requirements include resilient positioning, industry-standard data interfaces, remote configuration, monitoring, diagnostics, reporting, security and ongoing support throughout the solution lifecycle. Lot 1 - Part 2 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Solution Provision of a comprehensive onboard CCTV solution providing appropriate internal and external vehicle coverage for passenger safety, operational management and incident investigation. The solution shall support continuous high-quality recording, secure storage and retrieval, authorised access and evidential integrity. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required. Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. The solution shall provide reliable passenger-count data for operational, planning and passenger-information purposes and integrate with onboard and central systems. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation. Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support. Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. The solution shall support operational messaging, service information, alerts and emergency communications through an appropriate driver interface. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, secure communications, operational logging, remote configuration, equipment monitoring, diagnostics and resilient operation across the vehicle fleet. Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Solutions shall support appropriate front, side and rear displays, accessibility and visibility requirements and integration with onboard systems to automate displayed information. Requirements include remote configuration, operational overrides, equipment monitoring, diagnostics, secure communications, robust vehicle-grade equipment and ongoing maintenance and support. Lot 1 - Part 7 - Audio Visual Passenger Information (AVA) Solution Provision of an accessible onboard Audio Visual Passenger Information solution delivering automated visual and audible information concerning routes, destinations, next stops, disruptions and other relevant passenger messages. The solution shall integrate with vehicle location and onboard systems to trigger information accurately. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support. Lot 1 - Part 8 - Bridge Strike Prevention Solution Provision of an onboard Bridge Strike Prevention solution designed to reduce the risk of vehicles approaching or striking structures with insufficient clearance. The solution shall use vehicle dimensions together with accurate location, mapping and detection information to provide timely audible and visual driver warnings. Requirements include reliable hazard identification, minimisation of false alerts, offline resilience, secure updates, event logging, diagnostics and onboard-system integration. Lot 1 - Part 9 - Vehicle Compute Capability (VCC) Solution Provision of a robust onboard Vehicle Compute Capability providing a shared computing platform for hosting, integrating and managing multiple vehicle applications and data services. The solution shall provide sufficient processing capacity, storage and future scalability while supporting secure application separation and interoperability. Requirements include edge processing, secure communications, remote software management, monitoring and diagnostics, onboard-system integration and future expansion throughout its operational lifecycle. Lot 2 is for Franchising and Wider Transport Ticketing & Payment Consultancy Services. It has 6 Parts: Lot 2 - Part 1 - Franchised Bus Scheme Development and Implementation Support The provision of specialist consultancy services to support the development, assessment and implementation of bus franchising schemes. Services may include business cases, network and commercial design, financial modelling, consultation, procurement, mobilisation, integrated fares and ticketing, assets and technology, contract management, service permits, independent assurance and stakeholder engagement. Lot 2 - Part 2 - Transport Ticketing Management Policy Advice The provision of strategic, policy and management consultancy relating to transport ticketing and payment systems. Services may encompass ITSO, Stored Value, contactless EMV, barcode and QR ticketing, Account Based and Multi-Token Ticketing, Mobility as a Service, and wider ticketing initiatives across public-sector authorities, transport operators and national organisations. Lot 2 - Part 3 - Transport Ticketing Technical & Revenue Scheme Delivery The provision of technical consultancy and delivery support for transport ticketing schemes, including development of technical specifications, implementation and integration of ITSO and other ticketing technologies, Electronic Ticket Machines and ticketing readers. Services may also include management of multi-platform implementations and development of technical solutions through engagement with relevant stakeholders. Lot 2 - Part 4 - Transport Ticketing Governance, Research and Competitive Bidding Services The provision of specialist support relating to transport ticketing governance, research, procurement and competitive funding or bidding activities. Services may include governance advice for public and commercial organisations, preparation of grant, tender and franchise submissions, support for public procurement exercises, and research activities contributing to sustainable transport policy and delivery. Lot 2 - Part 5 - Entitlement (Concessionary) Travel Management Services The provision of management, policy and project support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, with particular emphasis on revenue reimbursement and apportionment. Services may include multi-operator and multimodal schemes, multiple ITSO HOPS and Customer Management Systems, and schemes operating across multiple ticketing channels, technologies and participating organisations. Lot 2 - Part 6 - Technical Entitlement (Concessionary) Support Services The provision of specialist technical support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, including reimbursement implementation, revenue modelling and apportionment, ETM data analysis, national reimbursement guidance and alternative allocation methodologies. Services may also encompass auditable datasets, payment reporting, stakeholder-led revenue solutions and expert technical evidence supporting appeals, tribunals or legal proceedings.
